summary: A very large eastern Bangkok lake park for walking, cycling and organised water sports. The park is free; access to sailing, windsurfing, kayaking, canoeing and SUP depends on sports-center membership and advance booking.
whyGo: Get space, greenery and a long lakeside loop away from central Bangkok’s busiest sights.
Try a BMA-run water-sports centre offering sailing, windsurfing, kayaking, canoeing and stand-up paddleboarding, with lessons listed.
bestFor: Cyclists, runners, families and visitors wanting an outdoor half-day.
Water-sports enthusiasts willing to arrange membership and a session in advance.
skipIf: You want a central Bangkok attraction or an easy last-minute water activity.
You need confirmed step-free access or detailed accessible facilities; published accessibility information is limited.
duration: Allow 1–2 hours for a walk or ride; plan 2–3 hours if arranging a water-sports session. These are planning estimates.
cost: Park admission is free. BMA lists annual aquatic-center membership for foreign visitors at ฿300 for ages 8–60 and ฿150 for 61+; confirm whether any equipment or session charges apply. The city learning portal lists other age bands and Thai rates, so check directly if relevant.
hours: BMA’s Greener Bangkok park page lists daily 04:30–18:30, including cycling hours. It lists water-sports sessions 12:00–14:30 and 15:00–18:00. Another BMA city portal gives sports-center hours as weekdays 08:30–19:30 and weekends/holidays 10:30–19:30, a discrepancy worth confirming by phone (+66 2 328 0236).
bestTime: Go early for cooler walking or cycling. Choose a water-sports session only after confirming availability and reservation requirements.
gettingThere: The park is on Chaloem Prakiat Rama 9 Road, Soi 43, Prawet. BMA lists bus 206 to the Soi 43 entrance followed by a songthaew, or BTS Udom Suk then a red bus from the entrance of Udom Suk Alley. A taxi or ride-hail is simpler for the final leg; public-transport services and connections should be checked on the day. Parking is listed on site.
booking: No booking is stated for park entry. For water sports, BMA says to register for membership and reserve through the CSTD application. Contact the centre at +66 2 328 0236 to confirm foreign-member registration, session times, equipment charges and December availability before making the trip.
accessibility: The BMA page confirms a lake loop, sports facilities, toilets and parking but does not describe step-free routes, accessible toilets, mobility-device suitability or accessible water-sports provision. Call the center to check specific needs.
practicalTips: Treat this as a destination outing in Prawet rather than a quick stop from central Bangkok.
Bring sun protection and water; exposed sections of the lake loop may feel hot even in the morning.
Cycling is listed on a 4.2 km route; ask locally about bike rental or bring your own, as current rental details are not confirmed.
Observe the park’s stated no-drone and no-smoking rules.
decemberNotes: December is within Bangkok’s cooler, generally drier season, making an early outdoor visit a sensible plan. Water-sports dates, operational hours and reservation capacity for December 2026 are not published as a dated schedule; verify shortly before visiting. Park closing is early evening, so do not plan a late sunset visit.
uncertainties: BMA sources show different opening hours for the park and sports center; call to confirm which applies to your activity and day.
The current foreign-member fee is published, but separate equipment/session charges and membership-document requirements are not clear.
Accessible routes and facilities are not described in the official listing.
The linked BMA photo page does not identify a photographer or reuse license; permission is not established.
